title: The Morning Post
brief: Four messages reached the gatehouse overnight. Two are ordinary. Two are not. Decide which is which.
sandboxNotice: These messages are fabricated for training. No mailbox is read, no link is live, and no address here belongs to a real person or organisation.
objectiveText: Inspect the headers, the links and the attachments, then give a verdict on each.
hints: Compare the display name against the actual address, and the From against the Reply-To.
Hover intent: read where a link actually points, not what it says.
Urgency plus a request for credentials or payment is the oldest shape in the trade.
Not every message with an attachment is hostile. Over-blocking has a cost too.
debrief: The two hostile messages lean on different levers. One forges a trusted internal sender and routes replies elsewhere, with a link whose visible text and real destination disagree. The other manufactures urgency about a payment and attaches a document with a double extension. The two legitimate messages are deliberately unremarkable: one has an attachment and one has an external sender, because a triage exercise where every suspicious-looking signal is hostile teaches you to over-block. Reporting a genuine invoice as phishing has a real cost.

emails.subject: Rota for next week

headers.name: Received-SPF
headers.value: pass (gatehouse.yahrah.local: domain of oribe@gatehouse.yahrah.local designates 192.168.10.5 as permitted sender)

emails.body:
Rota attached for next week. I have you on north post Tuesday and Thursday. Shout if that clashes with the training day.

Oribe
tells: SPF passes and DKIM is valid for the sending domain.
The attachment is a plain .csv with a single, expected extension.
No urgency, no credential request, no link.

emails.subject: URGENT: re-verify your gatehouse account before 09:00

headers.name: Received-SPF
headers.value: fail (gatehouse.yahrah.local: domain of sagae@gatehouse.yahrah.local does not designate 203.0.113.9 as permitted sender)

emails.body:
Our records show your gatehouse credentials expire this morning. Re-verify now or your access will be suspended at 09:00 and you will need to attend in person to restore it.

Verify here: https://gatehouse.yahrah.local/verify

Sagae
tells: SPF fails: the sending host is not permitted to send for that domain.
Reply-To and Return-Path point to an external domain that merely resembles the real one.
The link text and the actual destination disagree.
Manufactured deadline, and a demand to re-enter credentials.

emails.subject: Overdue invoice - immediate payment required
emails.body: Your account is overdue. The attached statement must be settled today to avoid suspension of supply. Open the attachment for payment details.
tells: The attachment has a double extension: .pdf.scr is an executable, not a document.
The Return-Path domain uses a capital I in place of the l in 'supply'.
Urgency and a threat of service suspension to rush the decision.

emails.subject: Delivery window for the lamp oil order
emails.body:
Morning. We can deliver the lamp oil Thursday between 10 and 12, or Friday first thing. Let me know which suits and I will book it in.

Kiri
tells: External sender, but SPF passes and DKIM is valid for its own domain.
Return-Path matches the From address exactly.
No urgency, no credentials requested, no link or attachment.
External does not mean hostile: this is an ordinary supplier reply.
